title: Modernism: Make It New
objective: After this level you can explain why writers after World War I broke with traditional plots and forms.
summary: After World War I shook faith in Western culture, modernists broke old forms. Pound's slogan was Make It New; Joyce's Ulysses (1922) turned Homer's Odyssey into one ordinary Dublin day.

cards.headline: Modernism came to be summed up as "Make it new." The phrase itself was ancient.
cards.body: Ezra Pound used Make It New as the title of a 1934 book of essays, and decades later it became the label for modernist newness. He took it from a Chinese anecdote: Tang, first king of the Shang dynasty, was said to have had the words inscribed on his washbasin. So what were modern writers trying to make new, and why then?

cards.headline: A war that broke the old forms
cards.body: Modernism was a period of experiment in the arts, running from the late 19th to the mid-20th century. As a literary movement, though, it belongs above all to the years after World War I (1914 to 1918). The war's sheer enormity undermined faith in the foundations of Western society and culture, and postwar writing filled with disillusionment and fragmentation. If the world had broken into pieces, why should a story arrive in one neat piece?

cards.headline: What they broke
cards.body: Modernist writers challenged the conventions not just of their parents' day but of the whole post-Romantic era. Their experiments were radical. Stream of consciousness followed the flow of a mind instead of a tidy plot. Poems were assembled from fragmentary images and allusions. And readers were expected to take an active role in working out what it all meant. The story no longer came with a tour guide.

cards.headline: 1922: an ordinary day as an epic
cards.body: The landmark year was 1922, when both T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land and James Joyce's Ulysses appeared. Ulysses, first published in Paris, follows three Dubliners through a single day, June 16, 1904. It runs parallel to Homer's Odyssey: Leopold Bloom is Odysseus, Stephen Dedalus is Telemachus, and Molly Bloom is Penelope. The point: an ordinary modern life deserves the same attention as a hero's.

questions.prompt: Where did Ezra Pound's modernist slogan "Make it new" come from?

options.label: A line in Homer's Odyssey
options.rationale: Joyce borrowed from the Odyssey; Pound's phrase was Chinese.

options.label: A Chinese anecdote about a king's inscribed washbasin
A recruiting poster from World War I
options.rationale: It was far older than the war.

options.label: The last page of Joyce's Ulysses
options.rationale: Pound's phrase came from ancient China.

questions.explanation: Pound took Make It New from an anecdote about Tang, first king of the Shang dynasty, who had the words inscribed on his washbasin.

questions.prompt: A novel from the 1920s tells its story in scattered pieces with no tidy ending. By Level 81's account, what is it most likely reflecting?

options.label: Confidence that society was steadily improving
options.rationale: The war had shaken that confidence.

options.label: A wish to copy the neat plots of earlier novels
Postwar disillusionment and a sense of fragmentation
A rule that every story must follow one hero
options.rationale: Modernists broke rules; they didn't add this one.

questions.explanation: World War I undermined faith in Western society and culture, and postwar modernist writing reflects disillusionment and fragmentation, often in broken forms.

questions.prompt: Joyce rebuilt the Odyssey around ordinary Dubliners. Which habit of Homer's own singers (Level 6) does that most resemble?

options.label: Pressing every line into clay tablets
options.rationale: That's how Gilgamesh survived, not Homer.

options.label: Refusing to repeat any phrase or scene
options.rationale: They reused formulas and type-scenes constantly.

options.label: Reshaping inherited stories and scenes their own way

questions.explanation: Homer's singers inherited phrases, scenes and plots and reshaped them in performance. Joyce did the same with the Odyssey.
